articles.headline: datasette-llm 0.1a9 ships with automatic model selection
articles.dek: Version 0.1a9 adds a default‑model hook for the Datasette Agent and tags the agent for cleaner pipelines.

body.text: Key Takeaway

The 0.1a9 bump makes the Datasette Agent automatically pick the configured LLM instead of requiring explicit model arguments, and it adds built‑in tags so your queries can be filtered by "datasette‑llm" and "datasette‑agent" without extra code [FACT:f76a2189d5bfa4a3a37f0cd510d1f182][FACT:6865546e0635ffb405125bc4b0f5d2be][FACT:362dc48b5193c70c711c8f1d891dba1a].
Why This Matters

For builders, fewer boilerplate lines mean faster prototyping and fewer runtime mismatches—especially when you’re stitching together multiple agents that need to agree on which model to call. The new tags also let you route logs or metrics by component without custom naming schemes [FACT:6865546e0635ffb405125bc4b0f5d2be][FACT:362dc48b5193c70c711c8f1d891dba1a].
What Happened

Simon Willison announced the 0.1a9 release on Oct 31, 2026, noting that the package now ships a "default model" flag for the Datasette Agent and three canonical tags: "datasette‑llm", "datasette‑agent", and a generic "tag" marker for orchestration tools [FACT:f76a2189d5bfa4a3a37f0cd510d1f182][FACT:362dc48b5193c70c711c8f1d891dba1a].
Builder View

If you already run a Datasette‑backed API, upgrade to 0.1a9 and drop the manual `model=` arguments from your endpoint definitions. Your CI can now verify that every request carries the correct tag, which simplifies monitoring dashboards and reduces the risk of sending a query to the wrong model during a multi‑agent rollout [FACT:6865546e0635ffb405125bc4b0f5d2be][FACT:362dc48b5193c70c711c8f1d891dba1a].
Open Questions

The release notes don’t detail performance impact; early adopters will need to benchmark against the previous 0.1a8, especially on edge hardware where LLM inference can vary. Related work on scaling multi‑agent orchestration suggests that tighter coupling like this can alleviate bottlenecks, but Snapdragon X2 Elite users have reported up‑to‑87 % slower LLM throughput after driver updates, so hardware compatibility remains a question [FACT:555312ae8505b15672558d8a9440ffb2][FACT:ccf27fc2f81e7149517d0cd26ecebe05].
Ardur Take

Two independent sources confirm the same feature set, giving this update a high confidence rating. If your stack already uses Datasette Agent, the upgrade is a low‑effort win that cleans up config and improves observability; otherwise, keep an eye on the next minor release for any performance tweaks [FACT:f76a2189d5bfa4a3a37f0cd510d1f182][FACT:6865546e0635ffb405125bc4b0f5d2be].

keyPoints: datasette‑llm 0.1a9 introduces a default‑model flag for the Datasette Agent.
Three new tags (datasette‑llm, datasette‑agent, generic) enable easier query routing and monitoring.
Upgrade removes the need to manually specify the LLM in each endpoint definition.
articles.whyItMatters: Automatic model selection and standardized tags cut down on configuration errors and give you clearer telemetry, which translates into faster iteration cycles for any AI‑powered service built on Datasette.
articles.readerAction: Pull the 0.1a9 package via pip (`pip install datasette-llm==0.1a9`), remove any explicit `model=` arguments from your agent configs, and verify that your logging pipeline captures the new tags.

articles.headline: Open‑source security in the AI exploit era: Patch without changing a thing
articles.dek: A zero‑touch webhook lets you seal AI‑model vulnerabilities in Kubernetes clusters without rebuilding containers.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Open‑source tooling now delivers runtime patches for Kubernetes that neutralize AI model exploits while leaving your container images untouched, saving you rebuild time and reducing blast radius. [FACT:ff90b5930f126785b8b5e8d1bf4c08ec][FACT:520e3395a967d3638acfa764003b9b40]
Why This Matters

AI‑driven services are being weaponized faster than a CI pipeline can catch them, with exploit attempts landing before the code even merges. A slip‑in patch at the orchestration layer buys you a critical window to protect workloads without a full redeploy cycle. [FACT:032605ae851f65ff480dc8cd7be9aec0][FACT:520e3395a967d3638acfa764003b9b40]
What Happened

The community project Glasswing rolled out a kube‑admission webhook that rewrites pod security policies on the fly, sandboxing model calls and wiping out the freshest model‑diff attack that surfaced within hours of discovery. The fix lives entirely in the webhook, so no image change is required. [FACT:0d62eecf43be2dd63e93e3bcacf27fd1][FACT:7790a5e98df9d25abd60af602099eacb]
Builder View

For Kubernetes builders, enabling the webhook is a single Helm value change; you get immediate mitigation against the latest model‑diff exploit while preserving existing Helm charts, CI pipelines, and rollout strategies. No rebuild, no downtime, just a safer surface. [FACT:7790a5e98df9d25abd60af602099eacb]
Open Questions

Can the webhook keep pace with the torrent of new model‑diff exploits emerging from Anthropic and other vendors? Will the added admission‑control checks impact cluster latency at scale? The community has yet to publish performance benchmarks. [FACT:826d233402aca3e020adc3ed70ddb7c7][FACT:032605ae851f65ff480dc8cd7be9aec0]
Ardur Take

Open‑source got the first hit, but it also delivered the fastest remediation. Deploy the webhook now as a stop‑gap shield, then watch for hardened, model‑aware runtimes to replace it. Treat this as a temporary safety net, not a permanent security model. [FACT:ff90b5930f126785b8b5e8d1bf4c08ec]

keyPoints: Zero‑touch webhook patches AI model vulnerabilities at the Kubernetes layer.
No container rebuild needed – a single Helm flag activates protection.
The fix responds to model‑diff exploits that appear within hours of discovery.
articles.whyItMatters: Kubernetes clusters running AI services face a new race‑condition: exploits appear before you can ship a new image. A runtime patch gives operators a usable defense without breaking existing CI/CD flow.
articles.readerAction: Add the Glasswing admission webhook to your cluster, enable the "secureModelCalls" flag in your Helm values, and monitor the audit log for blocked model‑diff attempts.
